A survey question is biased when it leads the respondent (“Don’t you agree…”, loaded words such as harmful, boring, delicious), forces a choice between only some answers, or asks two things at once. An unbiased question is neutral and open.
“Don’t you agree that reading is the best way…” pushes the respondent to agree.
Answer.
